name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh known primarily as the father of Iddo. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional notes expanding on his life or ministry. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation and paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'YHWH remembers' in Hebrew. This proper name, though not given by God directly, reflects a common theophoric element emphasizing God's faithfulness and memory. The biblical record does not attribute any special titles to him beyond his given name.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Manasseh and as the father of Iddo. These relationships are drawn directly from Scripture, with no further family connections recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Manasseh and as the father of Iddo. This connection situates him within the broader history of Israel's tribes and leadership lines, contributing to the continuity of God's covenant people. Though not prominent in other events, his mention affirms the faithfulness of God's promises through successive generations.
